To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have determined the structure of a unique member of the PIN superfamily of nuclease domains and have shown that it is a functional tRNA 5′ processing enzyme.

The crystal structure of a protein only ribonuclease (PRORP1) from the plant Arabidopsis thalanica reveals a unique domain architecture that includes an NYN metallo nuclease and a pentatricopeteptide repeat (PPRs) domain that are connected by a zinc binding domain.

the crystal structure of a protein only ribonuclease reveals a novel PIN domain like fold that evolved recently from an RNA based enzyme, and that this protein is a ribonuclease that is active with a pre-tRNA bound to its PPR domain.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular basis for the evolution of catalysis and the origin and evolution of the genetic code.
understanding the evolution of catalysis in the context of the RNA world and the transition to the protein dominated world.
the molecular mechanisms of tRNA maturation and how they evolved.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the structure of PRORPs provides insight into the evolutionary transition from an RNA world to a protein world, and that this transition was facilitated by the development of a catalytic strategy that allowed the RNA component of RNase P to be replaced by a metal binding protein.
this structure provides a framework for understanding the evolution of catalysis from RNA to protein.
this work provides a structural basis for understanding the evolution of catalysis and the differences between protein and RNA catalysts.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have solved the structure of a novel protein domain that is related to a family of nucleases, the FLAP nulceases, that is involved in RNA maturation.

we have solved the structure of a protein that is a member a family of enzymes that process precursor tRNas in organelles, we have identified the residues that are required for catalysis, and we have determined how the protein interacts with the pre-tRNA.
PRORP1 is the first structure of a PIN domain like fold protein and provides insight into the evolutionary relationship of the PIN superfamily and the FLAP family of proteins.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the PRORP1 structure provides a foundation for understanding the catalytic mechanism of this enzyme, the evolutionary relationship between PRORP and the FLAP family of nucleases and provides a molecular level comparison between the catalytic strategies employed by the only known natural evolved protein and RNA catalysts that perform pre tRNA maturing, a key step in tRNA biogenesis.
PRORP1 is an enzyme with a catalytic domain that has a unique fold that has evolved to catalyze a specific chemical reaction.
we have solved the crystal structure of a protein that is responsible for processing the 5' ends of tRNAs in plant mitochondria and chloroplasts.
